investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible peer-pod nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new remote-agent pods. Because the pod never started, the eval runner could not reach the agent creation API, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

failed-check.timing: check status=fail, latencyMs=136091, well within the outageLatencyMs=360000 threshold, confirming the failure was a hard scheduling block rather than a timeout.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was captured, consistent with the pod never starting.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error message, pod stuck for 145s, no evidence collected.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or leaked pods, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling attempts. Preemption was also ruled out ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

[Likely] Node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, concentrating all remote-agent scheduling pressure onto only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or stale, capacity appears lower than the physical cluster size.

[Possible] Leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user sessions did not clean up pods, the resource quota could be exhausted by non-running workloads.
[Possible] Cluster scaling has not provisioned additional peer-pod-capable nodes to meet demand, and the current 2-node pool is undersized for concurrent eval and production load.

investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes do not match the affinity/selector at all. With no preemption victims available and no matching nodes with free VM slots, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or source-code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: because createAgent (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returns a live agent, no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is ever written, and the expected-output contract defined in check-expectations.json line 264 is fully violated.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or label drift: the four remaining nodes may have lost the label required by the remote-agent pod spec, reducing the eligible node pool to only two nodes and amplifying the capacity problem. Supported by the '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' clause in failed-check.message.

investigation.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI API Credit Balance Exhausted on /api/generate/image/stream
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to return a credit_balance_exhausted error. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame, and no image URL was produced, causing both contract assertions to fail. This is an eval infrastructure credential/billing issue, not a user-facing product outage.
investigation.rootCause: The OpenAI API account associated with the eval runner's credentials has exhausted its credit balance (error code: credit_balance_exhausted, type: insufficient_quota). When the runner called /api/generate/image/stream, the backend forwarded the request to OpenAI, received the quota error, and emitted a generation_error frame with code GENERATION_FAILED. Because the stream never reached a successful completion, the generation_completed frame was never emitted and no image URL was produced. Both required contract assertions — frameTypes contains "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equals true — failed as a direct consequence of the upstream billing failure, not a code defect in the eval runner or the image generation route itself.

failed-check.evidence: The observed frameTypes sequence is [generation_start, generation_start, generation_progress, generation_error, message] — generation_completed is absent, and imageUrlPresent is false, directly matching both assertion failures.

The API returned credit_balance_exhausted synchronously, preventing any image from being generated. This is the direct and most strongly evidenced cause.

Secondary — Wrong or misconfigured API key used by the eval runner: The runner may be using an API key scoped to an organization or project that has a separate, depleted credit pool, while a different key with available credits exists. The error message points to the billing page for the organization owning the key in use.

investigations.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI API Credit Balance Exhausted on /api/generate/image/stream
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to return a credit_balance_exhausted error. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame, and no image URL was produced, causing both contract assertions to fail. This is an eval infrastructure credential/billing issue, not a user-facing product outage.
investigations.rootCause: The OpenAI API account associated with the eval runner's credentials has exhausted its credit balance (error code: credit_balance_exhausted, type: insufficient_quota). When the runner called /api/generate/image/stream, the backend forwarded the request to OpenAI, received the quota error, and emitted a generation_error frame with code GENERATION_FAILED. Because the stream never reached a successful completion, the generation_completed frame was never emitted and no image URL was produced. Both required contract assertions — frameTypes contains "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equals true — failed as a direct consequence of the upstream billing failure, not a code defect in the eval runner or the image generation route itself.
proof: failed-check.message: The check message contains the verbatim OpenAI error: {"type": "insufficient_quota", "code": "credit_balance_exhausted", "message": "You have no credits remaining. Add credits to continue using the API at https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/billing/."}.

failed-check.evidence: The observed frameTypes sequence is [generation_start, generation_start, generation_progress, generation_error, message] — generation_completed is absent, and imageUrlPresent is false, directly matching both assertion failures.

failed-check.evidence: The generation_error frame carries data.code=GENERATION_FAILED and data.message containing the full OpenAI insufficient_quota error body, confirming the error originated from the OpenAI API call, not from eval runner logic.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1380 — the call returned in under 1.4 seconds, far below the warningLatencyMs threshold of 180000ms, consistent with an immediate API rejection rather than a timeout or slow generation failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1978-1986: The runner calls apiSse(args, "/api/generate/image/stream", { prompt: ..., model: process.env.AURA_STATUS_IMAGE_MODEL || "gpt-image-2" }) — the model gpt-image-2 is an OpenAI image generation model, confirming the dependency on an OpenAI-billed API key.

expected-output.contract: The contract requires frameTypes to contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent to equal true — neither condition can be satisfied when the upstream OpenAI call is rejected at the billing layer before image generation begins.
possibleCauses: Primary — OpenAI API credit balance exhausted: The eval runner's OpenAI API key (or the organization account it belongs to) has run out of prepaid credits. The API returned credit_balance_exhausted synchronously, preventing any image from being generated. This is the direct and most strongly evidenced cause.

Secondary — Wrong or misconfigured API key used by the eval runner: The runner may be using an API key scoped to an organization or project that has a separate, depleted credit pool, while a different key with available credits exists. The error message points to the billing page for the organization owning the key in use.

Tertiary — Eval runner environment variable AURA_STATUS_IMAGE_MODEL or the API key secret is misconfigured for the desktop-nightly-macos-aarch64 environment, causing it to use a key with no quota rather than the intended key. This is less likely given the error is a clear billing rejection, but cannot be ruled out without inspecting the runner's secret configuration.

investigations.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returns 502/424 provider_account_unavailable
investigations.summary: The model-matrix eval failed because the model aura-gpt-5-5 returned a 502 Bad Gateway wrapping a 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable, causing 1 of 2 configured models to fail and violating the allPassed=true and failedModelCount=0 assertions in the expected-output contract. The sibling model aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 passed cleanly, isolating the failure to the aura-gpt-5-5 provider path only.
investigations.rootCause: The AURA runtime harness was unable to reach the upstream model provider for aura-gpt-5-5 at the time of the eval run (2026-08-10T18:52:10Z). The API gateway returned HTTP 502 containing a nested 424 Failed Dependency with code provider_account_unavailable and the message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits." This is a provider-side or gateway-side availability failure scoped to the aura-gpt-5-5 route, not a misconfiguration of the eval harness or a code regression. The eval infrastructure itself is functioning correctly: all required evidence fields were present, the runner executed both models, and the passing model returned the expected phrase.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes

investigations.rootCause: The snapshot file at the published URL was not refreshed within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot's source field reports "desktop-nightly-release" rather than "github-actions", indicating the snapshot was last written by a desktop nightly release process rather than the scheduled GitHub Actions workflow. The most likely operational cause is that the workflow or process responsible for regenerating and publishing status.json did not run or did not complete successfully in the ~5 hours preceding the eval run at 2026-08-10T19:00:12Z, leaving a 343-minute-old artifact in place.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all passed — isolates the failure to the snapshot JSON freshness, not the public website infrastructure.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: check registered as required=false, statusImpact='informational', staleAfterMinutes=360 — the registry staleness threshold (360 min) is looser than the eval contract threshold (300 min), meaning the eval contract is the binding freshness gate.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2164-2172: runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and passes it through statusSnapshotEvidence() — the eval correctly read the live published file.
possibleCauses: Most likely: The scheduled workflow or automated process that publishes status.json did not execute or did not complete in the ~5 hours before the eval ran, leaving the previous desktop-nightly-release snapshot in place beyond the 300-minute contract limit.

Secondary: The snapshot generation workflow ran but failed to push/publish the updated status.json to the GitHub Pages path (https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json), so the stale file remained.

Tertiary: The snapshot generation schedule is misaligned — if the publishing cadence is longer than 300 minutes (e.g., every 6 hours), the eval contract will fail on every cycle near the boundary even when the workflow runs normally.

Lower confidence: A transient CDN or GitHub Pages caching delay caused the eval to read a stale cached version of status.json even though a fresh file had been published. This is less likely given the 43-minute overage.
